sentences.text: Eurhinosaurus was an extinct genus of ichthyosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic period.
Adult individuals could reach a length of 7 meters, making them large animals.
The animal possessed a fish-like fusiform body with a well-developed dorsal fin, hypocercal caudal fin, paired fins, and remarkably large eyes.
As a reptile, this creature breathed using lungs rather than gills.
Its skull featured an elongated upper jaw that was twice as long as the lower jaw.
The mouth contained delicate, sharply pointed teeth with smooth enamel that pointed to the sides, resembling a sawfish.
A Miocene cetacean named Eurhinodelphis independently evolved a similar jaw structure.
The animal possessed a large scleral ring in its eye, likely used to maintain eye shape against deep-sea pressure.
The species was first named Ichthyosaurus longirostris by Gideon Mantell in 1851.
The first skull of Eurhinosaurus longirostris was discovered by Richard Owen and Jaeger in Switzerland in 1856.
The genus Eurhinosaurus was erected in 1909 by Abel to separate Ichthyosaurus longirostris based on its abbreviated mandible.
The species E. huenei, described in 1930, was resurrected to replace the dubious E. longirostris.
A second species, E. quenstedti, was described from Germany in 2022.
A third species, E. mistelgauensis, was described by Spicher et al. in 2025.
Eurhinosaurus was a high-speed swimmer that used lateral oscillations of its caudal fluke for propulsion in a thunniform swimming style.
Researchers suggest Eurhinosaurus may have used its jaw to violently spear prey to death, similar to swordfish, sailfish, or marlins.
Eurhinosaurus preyed on small, soft-bodied organisms including small fishes, oysters, and squid-like cephalopods.
Eurhinosaurus was likely a deep diver.
In the forefin, the radius bone was much larger than the ulna bone.
The genus Eurhinosaurus was named by Abel in 1909 and is classified within the family Leptonectidae.
Eurhinosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic Toarcian stage, between 183 and 175 million years ago.
Fossils of Eurhinosaurus have been found across Western Europe, including England, Germany, the Benelux, France, and Switzerland.
Eurhinosaurus inhabited the open ocean, living far from coastlines.
It is debated whether E. longirostris is a valid species, as it was replaced by the resurrected E. huenei due to poor preservation of the original type specimen.
